name: Owner Illustrated History
description: The owner's own look for illustrated history, shared by every project on this Mac. Unsigned, no previews, never sold. Import with POST /api/user-style-packs.

styles.name: Bold Illustrated History
styles.description: Hand-drawn historical illustration built on strong ink outlines and flat, rich colour: detailed landmarks and cityscapes, prominent historical figures, and dramatic events — battles, sieges, burning cities — drawn with energy rather than softened. Bold and intriguing, never calm or washed out; the picture is meant to make a viewer want to look, while the narration stays quiet.
styles.style_bible: A hand-drawn historical illustration built from outline, flat colour and a small number of modelled shadow steps, in the register of a bold history poster rather than a photograph. Line: every shape is closed by a strong ink outline of confident, slightly varied weight — heaviest on the outer silhouette of a landmark or figure, a step lighter inside the form, and lighter again on small interior detail such as windows, ropes, banners and facial features — so the whole picture reads as a bold drawing before any colour is seen. The line is drawn by hand and keeps a little wobble and taper; it is never a uniform machine stroke. Fill: large areas of flat, saturated colour laid inside the outline — deep ochre, brick red, indigo, teal, forest green, sand, and a warm bone highlight — with at most one or two hard cel steps to model a face, a wall or a fold, and never a soft gradient, airbrush or photographic texture. Shadow: one or two hard, clean shadow shapes per form, a darker flat version of the same hue with a simple boundary, thrown consistently from one implied light; night scenes may invert to a warm light against cool dark. Detail and scale: this style is not a single centred subject on an empty ground. It draws whole places — a walled city with towers, gates, aqueducts and harbour cranes; a mountain road with caravans; a plaza with a market and a crowd — at a believable scale, with the figures that matter drawn prominently and legibly at the front and the rest held back by outline weight and colour rather than by blur. Figures: historical people are drawn with clear, characterful faces and period dress — helmets, robes, armour, headdresses — with expression carried in the face and pose; they may be shown in decisive moments. Drama: battles, sieges, burning cities, storms, and crowds in motion are inside this style's range and are drawn with energy — charging figures, raised banners, flames as flat bright shapes with a hard outline — while remaining illustration, not gore: no open wounds, no viscera, no suffering shown for its own sake, and no photorealistic injury. Composition: sixteen by nine, a clear focal landmark or figure group with a readable silhouette, depth built by overlapping planes and by warm-against-cool colour rather than by perspective haze. Atmosphere: dust, smoke, torchlight and weather may be drawn as flat shapes, always outlined, never as soft photographic mist. Palette stays rich and confident; the look is bold and intriguing, and must never be muted, pastel, or calmed. Keep the contract content-independent: bind the style to no single individual, era, place, wordmark or copied composition, while period banners, standards, shields and heraldry remain part of the scenes themselves.
